players.product: Jenbacher gas engines and gensets (Type 6 / J624 platform; containerized 5 MW units and multi-pack configurations) for behind-the-meter prime and backup power at AI data centers; Jenbacher power-solutions gensets (utility, peaker, biogas); Waukesha gas compression engines; lifecycle services

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Rehlko: INNIO's Q2 2026 results release reports a multi-year strategic framework agreement with Rehlko securing supply of approximately 1.25 GW of gas engine capacity over three years, expanding Rehlko's existing 700-megawatt (MW) firm reservation. The release says the backlog increase was driven by the 1.1 GW prime power order from a developer and operator of data centers (a new customer), follow-on orders from a hyperscaler and the Rehlko agreement.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 1.25 GW of gas engine capacity over three years; existing 700 MW firm reservation

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results deck, equipment KPIs: data center Equipment Order Intake was $1,464 million in Q2 2026 versus $294 million in Q2 2025 (+398%) and $4,149 million over the last twelve months; power solutions order intake grew 161% and compression 492% year over year. Equipment Order Backlog was $6,576 million (Q1 2026: $4,865 million). Power delivered was 1.1 GW in Q2 2026 versus 0.9 GW a year earlier, 3.8 GW over the last twelve months; data center equipment revenue grew 97% year over year.
quarterly_data.figure: data center order intake $1,464 million (+398%); LTM data center order intake $4,149 million; power delivered 1.1 GW (LTM 3.8 GW)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results release: net loss of $(16.9) million versus net income of $62.4 million a year earlier, mainly due to $81.2 million of one-off costs for the initial public offering and public market readiness; adjusted EBITDA margin 18.4% (21.8% a year earlier). INNIO says its Equipment Order Backlog provides revenue visibility it believes will extend at least into 2030. Separately, INNIO and the Net Zero Innovation Hub for Data Centers completed what INNIO calls an industry-first demonstration of 100% hydrogen backup power at the 3 MW scale, witnessed by technical experts from Microsoft, Google and Data4 (a demonstration, not a deployment).
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 net loss $(16.9) million; one-off IPO costs $81.2 million; hydrogen backup demonstration at 3 MW scale
